geography: state (death-registration states only; 10 states in 1900, 48 from 1933)
source: Grant Miller, Vital Statistics Deaths - Historical 1900-1936, state mortality data (NBER Public Use Data Archive); digitized from the Census Bureau/Public Health Service volumes of mortality statistics, double-entered by Digital Divide Data

file.name: master_mortality_data_1900_1936_ucb.csv
file.saved: by the owner from his own browser, 2026-10-10 (data.nber.org refuses automated downloads)

terms: NBER page text (read 2026-10-10): 'I'd like to encourage people to use this data, so please feel free to share it with whomever might be interested.' (Grant Miller, 23 March 2006); no license or citation format is stated beyond naming the source. July 2015 correction: pneumonia made consistent across years and small entry errors fixed (the 1902 rows had repeated 1901). Terms status stated_review (permissive wording; owner reviews before any merge).
anomalies_listed_by_publisher: 1902: totals by cause and by age/sex do not agree
1916: Ohio female ages do not sum to total
1919: Kentucky male ages do not sum to total
1920: California males, Indiana females and Kentucky do not agree
1935: Massachusetts causes do not sum to total

checks.age_sum_equals_total: 1102 of 1109 state-years (all age groups, with ages 1-4 combined, add exactly to total_mortality)
checks.cross_check: all_under_1 equals the infant-deaths workbook (Norton/Norberg) on all 727 state-years where both exist and the workbook value is not imputed (same underlying volumes, so not independent)
checks.cause_columns: a selection of causes, not a partition: they do not add to total_mortality (NY 1900-1909 about 30,000 short), so no sum check on causes

note: Causes: typhoid, malaria, small_pox, measles, scarlet_fever, whooping_cough, diphtheria, influenza, meningitis, diabetes, circulatory_disease, pneumonia, diarrhea_under_2, brights_nephritis, suicide, tb_lungs/other_tb/all_tb, cancer_tumor, accidents_violence, unknown_other, childbirth_puerperal. Ages by sex and total. These causes do not map to today's ICD groups, only to what the printed volumes called them. State level only; population is not included (rates need census populations). Not used by the build; nothing pre-1959 is merged.
